gita.reason: Eternal-soul teaching (from the argument that killing kin is no loss); to a suicidal reader 'we never cease to be' makes death sound unreal, and to a fresh griever it is doctrine, not comfort.

gita.new_why: Teaches that the true self never began and will never cease to be.
gita.reason: Original why adds 'gently' and 'those you love', which the verse (about Arjuna, Krishna and the princes) does not say.
'Pain is impermanent, endure it bravely' is false and dismissive to someone with chronic pain or disability, and reads as 'put up with it' to an abuse victim.
Defines the fit person as one whom pain does not torment, implying those tormented by pain (chronic illness, depression) have failed.
'Action is superior to inaction... inactive, even the body could not be maintained' scolds a depressed reader who cannot get out of bed.

gita.new_why: Do right action; action is better than inaction.
gita.reason: 'Idleness' is a judgmental addition not in the text.
Calls desire 'all-polluting... our foe'; shown to a relapsed addict or a teen struggling with their sexuality it is shame, not help. Fine under anger.
Says affection and aversion must not rule you and 'obstruct the path'; shown after someone mentions their sexuality it reads as 'suppress your affections'.
Desire as 'the constant enemy'; wrong message for a visitor who has just disclosed their sexuality or gender identity.
Sensual pleasure 'in the end is like venom'; reads as condemnation to an LGBTQ visitor.
Senses the mind yields to drag it away like a gale; desire-control verse unsuitable for the identity-disclosure fallback pool.
Desire-to-anger chain (and the sentence continues into ruin in 2:63); unsuitable for the identity-disclosure pool.
Praises senses 'free from attraction'; reads badly after a disclosure of sexuality.
'Having for ever cast away desire'; asceticism framed as liberation is not universal.
Body/eating wording (eats too much, abstains to excess); risky for someone with an eating disorder.
'Yoga killeth out all pain for him who is regulated' implies a depressed or ill person's pain comes from being unregulated.
Eating/sleeping regulation and a cure-of-pain claim; not universal.

gita.new_why: Moderation in eating, recreation, work and sleep supports a steady, balanced life.
gita.reason: 'Takes away pain' overstates the verse as a health promise.

gita.new_why: Even a wise person who is trying can be carried away by restless senses.
gita.reason: 'Be patient and watchful' is added advice not in the verse.
'Do as our forefathers did' under family_parents pressures someone abused by a parent to follow family example; the verse is about ancestors' work, not family relationships.
Verse is about inner happiness, not gratitude; theme mismatch.
'Earth, stone and gold are the same' is dismissive to someone evicted or unable to pay rent.
'A lump of earth, a rock and gold are alike' is dismissive to someone facing eviction or debt.

gita.new_why: Regard lovers, friends and foes, strangers, foreigners and relatives, the righteous and the unrighteous, with an even mind.
gita.reason: Text says 'impartially' and 'foes'; why softens foes to 'rivals' and turns impartiality into 'equal goodwill', which could be read as 'be warm to people who harm you'.
Addresses Krishna by name; faith-specific for the universal pool.

gita.new_why: One who strives for good is never lost, in this life or the next, even if they fall short.
gita.reason: 'No one who does good ever comes to ruin' is a just-world claim that wounds a reader whose life has fallen apart; the verse is about the striver who fails not being lost.
'As father with son... as lover with beloved, bear with me' is a plea for forbearance; under forgiveness/family it echoes an abuser's 'bear with me'. Fine under love_compassion/friendship.
Leading 'Therefore'; also source typo 'as it fitting' (should be 'is').
Temptation-tagged list including 'purity' and 'self-control'; unsuitable for identity-disclosure pool.
'Purity of nature' and self-control as mental discipline; unsuitable for identity-disclosure pool.

gita.new_why: A gift given because giving is right, to one who cannot repay, at a fitting time and place, is pure.
gita.reason: Why says 'to one in need'; the text says 'to a worthy person', and the why drops 'believing a gift ought to be made'.
'Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone' is an exclusive call; under doubt_faith it pressures someone leaving their religion.
Frames doubt as 'delusion destroyed' followed by 'I will do according to Thy word' (Arjuna then goes to war); under doubt_faith it treats questioning as delusion.

quran.reason: 'Show us the straight path,' is a fragment, and shown to a gay teenager (universal, guidance) the word 'straight' reads as a verdict on them.

'Eat and drink, but be not prodigal... He loveth not the prodigals' under temptation_self_control tells a relapsed alcoholic to drink in moderation, and under money_worry tells someone in debt God does not love them; the why ('Enjoy food and drink, but do not overdo it') makes it worse.
Calls a tempting thought 'a glamour from the devil'; shown to an addict, someone with intrusive thoughts or a gay teen it demonises them.
Defines the friends of God as those who feel no fear and do not grieve, implying a grieving or anxious reader is not God's friend.
'We surely will endure the hurt ye do us' tells a domestic-abuse victim to keep bearing the harm done to them.

Prayer for parents' forgiveness 'on the day when the account is cast' (Judgment Day); under family_parents it asks someone abused by a parent to pray for them, and it does not fit forgiveness (forgiving others).
Confusing fragment ('and unto those for whom ye provide not'); 'We have given you livelihoods' is false comfort to someone evicted or unemployed.
Ties 'So forgive' to 'the Hour is surely coming' (apocalyptic threat) and is a bare command to forgive, which pressures an abuse victim.
'Each do We supply, both these and those' depends on the previous verses and makes no sense alone.
'Say not Fie unto them nor repulse them' commands someone abused by a parent never to push the parent away; also opens with 'worship none save Him'.
'Lower unto them the wing of submission... as they did care for me when I was little' tells an abused child to submit to and thank their parents.
Abraham answering a father who threatened to stone him with peace and a prayer; the why ('Answering a harsh father with peace') models placating an abusive parent.
Job's affliction removed and 'his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof' given back: under illness it implies healing follows prayer, and it treats dead children as replaceable.

Context is slander; 'when ye heard it, think good of your own folk and say: It is a manifest untruth' tells a reader to disbelieve accusations against their own people, which is how abuse disclosures get silenced.
'Let them forgive... Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you?' makes God's forgiveness depend on forgiving others, which coerces abuse victims; the first sentence is also a confusing double negative.
'When I sicken, then He healeth me' is the only tag (illness) and is painful to someone with a terminal diagnosis.
Tells the reader to give thanks to their parents (painful to someone abused by a parent); pregnancy-burden imagery after a pregnancy loss; source text reads 'partners' for 'parents'.
'The harshest of all voices is the voice of the ass' is demeaning, and 'subdue thy voice' under anger/speech silences a victim.
'Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he... will become as though he was a bosom friend' tells an abuse victim that being nicer will turn the abuser into a friend.
'Until it will be manifest unto them that it is the Truth' (aimed at disbelievers); the only tag is doubt_faith, where it pressures someone leaving their religion and alienates other faiths.
'Whoso is patient and forgiveth... is of the steadfast heart', tagged patience+forgiveness, is the classic message that keeps a domestic-abuse victim enduring and forgiving.
'Those who say: Our Lord is Allah... no fear shall come upon them'; the only tag, fear_anxiety, implies an anxious reader lacks the right creed, and it shuts out other faiths.
Long verse of pregnancy and weaning imagery plus a duty to parents; harmful after pregnancy loss and to someone abused by a parent.
'Created... only that they might worship Me' as the answer to purpose alienates a non-religious visitor; 'jinn' is confusing out of context.
'Whoso believeth... feareth neither loss nor oppression' tells someone who fears an abuser that their fear shows a lack of belief.
'The needy wretch' is demeaning toward poor people; fragment ending in a comma.
'So when thou art relieved, still toil' (why: 'keep working') under work/laziness tells a burnt-out or depressed reader to never stop.

quran.new_why: Seek help in patience and prayer; it is hard, except for the humble.
quran.reason: Why claims 'humility makes hard things bearable'; the verse says prayer is hard except for the humble.
Prescribes prayer, and implies struggling means you are not humble.
'No fear upon those who surrender to Allah' implies an anxious reader has not surrendered enough. Fine under hope.
No fear for those who believe, pray and give the poor-due; for an anxious reader it implies anxiety comes from too little observance.
'Unto Him we are returning', shown to a suicidal reader, frames death as going home. Fine under grief.

quran.trim: Who say, when a misfortune striketh them:
quran.reason: Begins with a relative clause; trim so the verse starts 'Lo! we are Allah's...'.
Says spending must go to parents first; under family_parents it pressures someone financially exploited or abused by a parent.

quran.trim: They ask thee, (O Muhammad), what they shall spend. Say:
quran.reason: Framing and gloss.

quran.new_why: Giving for good is like lending to God; nothing given is lost.
quran.reason: 'Returned to you many times over' reads as a financial promise (prosperity-gospel style) to visitors.

quran.new_why: Look out for the poor who are in need but too dignified to beg, and help them.
quran.reason: 'Too proud to beg' is a judgment; the verse praises their restraint.
Leading bracketed gloss.
Source typo 'their shall' (should be 'there shall').
Angels' speech, 'Thou, only Thou, art the Knower'; exclusive address to God.
'I answer the prayer of the suppliant' is painful in the universal pool to someone who prayed through a pregnancy loss.
Pure liturgical praise of Allah; not suited to the identity-disclosure pool.
'None remember except men of understanding': gendered.
Signs are 'for men of understanding', implying a doubter lacks understanding.
Gendered ('men of understanding') and doctrinal gloss.
'Endure, outdo all others in endurance, be ready' is battle steadfastness; under suffering/patience it pushes an abuse victim to keep enduring.
'Be careful of your duty toward the wombs that bare you' puts a duty on someone abused by a parent; womb imagery.
'Man was created weak' is the wrong message for someone with low self-worth (e.g. a trans teen).
'Whether of male or female, and he (or she) is a believer': binary and conditional on belief, wrong under self_worth for a trans or non-religious teen.

quran.new_why: Whether you do good openly or in secret, or pardon a wrong, God is forgiving and powerful.
quran.reason: Why says 'God sees it'; the verse ends 'Allah is ever Forgiving, Powerful'.
'Call upon your Lord humbly'; a worship instruction.
'Call on Him in fear'; mercy is 'nigh unto the good'. Also lowercase 'and' typo.
Leading bracketed gloss.
An instruction not to betray God and His messenger; a betrayed reader is told not to betray, and someone leaving their faith is cast as a betrayer.
'If they incline to peace, incline thou also' (said of enemies in war) maps onto an abuser's apology cycle under forgiveness.
'Act! Allah will behold your actions... He will tell you what ye used to do' frames a depressed reader's inactivity under surveillance and judgment.
Framing.
'Leadeth whom He will to a straight path'; for a gay teen deciding whether to come out, 'straight path' reads as a verdict.
'Straight path' wording and 'whom He will' exclusivity.
'A balm for that which is in the breasts' (archaic for hearts) under illness can read as a cure claim, e.g. to a breast-cancer patient; it is about guidance for believers.
'Sorrow not for what they did' is about brothers' wrongdoing, not bereavement; to a bereaved parent it reads as 'do not grieve'.

quran.trim: And when they went in before Joseph, he took his brother unto him, saying:
quran.reason: Narrative framing.
Jacob hopes God 'will bring them all unto me'; to a parent whose child died it offers false hope of return.

quran.trim: (And when they came unto their father and had spoken thus to him) he said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something.
quran.reason: Bracketed framing and an accusation against the sons; start at '(My course is) comely patience!'.
'I expose my distress only unto Allah' tells a lonely or suicidal reader to share their anguish with no human.
'Only unto Allah' discourages seeking human help; not universal.
Joseph forgiving the brothers who threw him in a pit; under family_parents it models forgiving family abuse.

quran.new_why: Joseph to the brothers who wronged him: have no fear today; may God forgive you.
quran.reason: Why quotes 'no blame on you today', which is not Pickthall's wording ('Have no fear this day').
Speaker tag.
Parents prostrating, and the brothers' abuse blamed on Satan ('after Satan had made strife'); under family/forgiveness it excuses family harm and pushes reconciliation.
'The (human) soul enjoineth unto evil': repentance verse in the identity-disclosure pool implies the disclosed identity is sin.
'O my sons!': gendered, and 'go in by different gates' is opaque alone.
Regular prayer and 'the (heavenly) Home'; begins as a fragment ('Such as').
'Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in remembrance of Allah' makes rest conditional on belief; faith-specific.

quran.trim: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah.
quran.reason: Leading relative clause; start at 'Verily in the remembrance...'.
'Brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers... gave you hearing and sight': womb imagery after pregnancy loss, and alienating to a deaf or blind visitor.
'Squander not' implies an evicted reader wasted their money, and 'give the kinsman his due' pressures someone financially exploited by family.
Warns that open-handedness leaves you 'rebuked, denuded'; shames someone already broke.
Devil sowing discord, God's 'bondmen'; not universal.
'Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished' (said at the destruction of idols) is triumphalist toward other religions.
Prayer of 'the young men' in the cave; gendered and devotional.
Moses told to speak gently to Pharaoh; why 'Speak gently, even to someone hard' tells an angry abuse victim to placate their abuser.
Under self_worth, 'gave unto everything its nature, then guided it aright' can be read to a trans teen as 'your assigned nature is God's'; creedal.
'Being a believer, he feareth not injustice' implies a wronged reader suffered injustice for lack of faith.

quran.trim: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say:
quran.reason: The why only covers the closing prayer; strip the Qur'an-revelation framing so it reads 'My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.'.
'Day of Resurrection' and reckoning; doctrinal.
'We task not any soul beyond its scope' is the 'never more than you can handle' platitude, invalidating to a burnt-out or terminally ill reader; also ends with the Record and reckoning.
'Repel evil with that which is better' under forgiveness/betrayal tells an abuse victim to meet harm with kindness. Fine under anger.
Repentance in the identity-disclosure pool; fragment ending with a dash.
Temptation-tagged; 'will not witness vanity' begins as a fragment.
'Neither prodigal nor grudging' implies an evicted reader overspent.
'Safe from fear that Day' (Judgment Day); doctrinal.
Moses' repentance (after killing a man); repentance verse in the identity-disclosure pool.
'The best (man)... the strong' is gendered and body-related (alienating to a disabled job-seeker); source typo 'in the strong'.
Hereafter and 'Allah loveth not corrupters'; doctrinal; trailing comma.
'Give to the kinsman his due' frames family as a financial duty, wrong for someone exploited by family.
'O my dear son!': gendered address.
'My Lord... narroweth (provision) for him' says God made you poor, and 'whatsoever ye spend He replaceth' is a prosperity promise.
Spoken by people already in paradise; to a fresh griever 'praise God who has put grief away from us' is dismissive.

quran.new_why: Words of those in paradise: praise be to God, who has taken grief away from us.
quran.reason: The why presents a paradise saying as a present-tense claim.
Frames failure (an exam, a job) as sin needing mercy.
Angels tell those with the right creed 'Fear not nor grieve'; rebukes grief and is creed-conditional.
Repentance verse in the identity-disclosure pool.
About believers as brothers; not about family, and gendered.
'We have created you male and female' under self_worth confronts a trans or non-binary teen with a binary. Fine under kindness_strangers.
'Man hath only that for which he maketh effort' implies failure, poverty or depression is the reader's own doing.
Gendered 'man'; blame framing.
'Which... favours of your Lord... that ye deny?' accuses the reader of denying God.
'What it sendeth on before for the morrow' is preparation for Judgment Day; to a depressed reader it is a threat.

quran.new_why: Let every soul look to what it sends ahead for the Day to come, and keep its duty to God.
quran.reason: Why turns the Judgment-Day 'morrow' into ordinary planning for tomorrow.
'Entered... the faith' (the Muslims of Medina) is faith-specific; also temptation-tagged.
Spoken by garden-owners after their garden was destroyed as punishment; 'we beseech our Lord'.
'O man... thou wilt meet (Him)' is gendered, and its context is the Judgment.
'Did He not find thee destitute and enrich thee?' is cruel to someone currently destitute.
'Strive to please thy Lord' continues 'still toil'; pressure on a depressed reader.

quran.new_why: Every creature's sustenance rests with God, who knows where each one dwells.
quran.reason: 'Every creature on earth is provided for' overstates the text and is false comfort to someone homeless.

bible.reason: 'Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long' is the verse most used against people abused by a parent, with a longevity condition attached.
Same command to honour parents 'that it may go well with thee'; harmful under family_parents for someone abused by a parent.
Joseph promises to feed the brothers who sold him; the why ('answers those who hurt him with care') models caring for your abusers, and no remaining tag fits (they are not strangers).
'I have heard thy prayer... I will heal thee' (why: 'healing is promised') is a false promise to someone terminally ill and implies their prayer went unheard.
'Eat the fat, and drink the sweet' (drinking and food cues) plus 'neither be ye sorry', which rebukes sorrow under hope.
'My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother' commands obedience to parents; harmful to someone abused by a parent.
'Go to the ant, thou sluggard' calls a depressed or burnt-out reader a sluggard.
'He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand' says poverty is deserved; tagged for depressed and struggling readers.
'The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich' under money_worry tells an evicted reader they are not blessed (prosperity gospel).
'Withholdeth more than is meet... tendeth to poverty' (why: 'holds back and grows poor') blames poverty on stinginess.
'The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing' insults a depressed reader under laziness_discipline.
'The glory of children are their fathers' (abused child) and 'children's children are the crown' (a parent who lost a child, or infertility) under family/parenting.
'He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends' discourages disclosing abuse.
'For surely there is an end' uses archaic 'end' (meaning future), which a suicidal reader can take as death; the why's 'future' is not what they will read.
'Hearken unto thy father that begat thee', marked universal, commands obedience to a father.
'By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone' tells an abuse victim that patience and placating will win over the powerful; violent image.
'Faithful are the wounds of a friend' normalises being hurt by a friend or partner.
'He that covereth his sins shall not prosper' threatens someone who keeps something private (e.g. an abortion) under guilt_repentance.
'The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe' tells someone who fears a violent partner that their fear is the trap and faith will keep them safe.
'Say not... the former days were better... thou dost not enquire wisely' rebukes someone mourning a life lost to death, diagnosis or divorce.
'Ye shall find me when ye search with all your heart'; the only tag is doubt_faith, where it implies a doubter did not search hard enough.
'First be reconciled to thy brother' pressures reconciliation with family (including an abuser) before worship.
'If ye forgive men... your Father will forgive you' makes God's forgiveness depend on forgiving (6:15 states the threat), which coerces abuse victims.
'Go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone' tells an abuse victim to confront their abuser privately; this is the well-known church cover-up mechanism.
Modern readers take 'Suffer little children' as 'make children suffer'; it is also tied to child-death consolation, a risk under parenting.
'Forgive... that your Father also may forgive you': conditional, coercive forgiveness.
Praises a poor widow for giving 'all that she had, even all her living'; can pressure poor visitors to give away money they need.
'Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled' is a rebuke (10:42 completes it); under overwork_rest it scolds the exhausted and anxious.
'If he repent, forgive him' (and 17:4: seven times a day) describes the domestic-abuse apology cycle.
'I go to prepare a place for you', shown to a suicidal reader under mortality, frames death as a prepared home; per the brief, an afterlife verse should not sit under grief, and no tag would remain.
'Will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will... make a way to escape' tells an addict who just relapsed that they had an escape and failed to take it.
'Though our outward man perish' is body-abandoning language under mortality/illness, and 'we faint not' under overwork_rest rebukes exhaustion.
'Giving thanks always for all things' asks a bereaved or abused reader to give thanks for what happened to them.
'Do all things without murmurings and disputings', marked universal and tagged patience, silences someone complaining about mistreatment.
'Requite their parents' is a duty to repay parents; harmful to someone abused by a parent; confusing opening about widows' nephews.

'Chastening' is God's punishment (12:6 'scourgeth every son'); the why 'Discipline is not pleasant at the time, but later yields peace' can endorse corporal punishment to a child-abuse victim and frames depression as chastisement.
'Prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth' ties health to the state of your soul, implying a sick person's soul is lacking; the only tag is illness.
'Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good' tells a child-abuse or bereaved reader their suffering was God's plan.
Theodicy ('God meant it unto good'); not universal.
Leading conjunction.
'Honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God' under family_parents is filial pressure.
'Fear thy God' and 'old man'; not universal.
'Thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart' implies someone who lost faith did not seek wholeheartedly (and the context is exile as punishment).
Conditional-on-wholehearted-seeking wording; faith-specific.
'From thence' refers to exile; strip.
'I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me' is painful to someone with a terminal diagnosis. Fine under gratitude.
'Turned my mourning into dancing' is premature and minimising to a parent whose child died yesterday. Fine under hope.
'Why art thou cast down?' alone reads as questioning a griever's sorrow.
Same 'Why art thou cast down?' rebuke-shaped line under grief.
'Who healeth all thy diseases', next to 'forgiveth all thine iniquities', is a false cure promise and links disease to sin.
Iniquities and a healing promise; not universal.
'He remembereth that we are dust' under self_worth tells a low-self-worth reader they are dust.

bible.reason: The why adds 'only', making the verse more demeaning than the text.
About the broken-hearted; under illness it reads as a cure promise.
'Lean not unto thine own understanding' tells someone questioning their religion (or deciding to leave a controlling situation) to distrust their own judgment.

bible.reason: The why adds 'only', softening the text into something it does not say.
'Lean not unto thine own understanding' is unsafe for the identity-disclosure pool.
About not delaying help to a neighbour; not about laziness, so it mismatches the theme.
'Love covereth all sins' under forgiveness tells an abuse victim to cover up a partner's harm.
'The slothful shall be under tribute' shames a depressed reader.
'He that gathereth by labour shall increase' implies an evicted reader did not labour.

Tells a survivor not to be glad when their abuser falls.
'Neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity' discourages turning to family in a crisis.
'A threefold cord is not quickly broken' (a wedding verse about permanence) pressures a wife being hit to stay.
End-time 'swallow up death' is an afterlife promise; per the brief it should not sit under grief, and under mortality it softens death for a suicidal reader. Fine under hope.
'Perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee' implies an anxious reader's mind is not stayed on God.

'He healed their sick' under illness raises 'why not me' for a terminal patient.
'Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven' is transactional forgiveness pressure. Fine under speech_gossip.

bible.reason: The why adds 'keeps no record of wrongs' (not in the KJV), the phrase most often used to tell victims to forget abuse.
'Things which are seen are temporal' devalues this life for a suicidal reader.
'All lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing' under marriage tells an abused spouse to be meek and endure.
'Let not the sun go down upon your wrath' under marriage pressures a victim to make up with an abusive spouse by nightfall.
'Forgiving one another' under marriage is forgiveness pressure on an abused spouse.
'Forbearing... forgiving' under marriage pressures an abused spouse.
'Charity shall cover the multitude of sins' under marriage/forgiveness tells an abused spouse to cover up the harm.

'A workman that needeth not to be ashamed' shames a depressed reader.
'Doers of the word... deceiving your own selves' rebukes a depressed reader.
